about: Claimed typological correspondences, recorded as two independently annotated passage sequences. A motif is drawn from the fixed vocabulary below and must carry a verbatim ASV fragment; tools/typology.mjs rejects any reference that does not resolve and any quotation that is not present in the ASV verse it cites. Who asserts the correspondence is recorded, never assumed: 'scripture' means a verse states it, and that verse is given; 'tradition' means the classical typological literature reads it so, with no scriptural assertion. Nothing here measures whether a reading is true.

sources.scripture: A verse of Scripture asserts the correspondence; the asserting reference is given in each record.
sources.tradition: The classical typological literature, represented by Patrick Fairbairn, The Typology of Scripture (1845-47) and Ada Habershon, The Study of the Types (1898). Attributed to the tradition as a whole, not to a located page in either work.
